The '''2004 World Championship''' was the 9th Star Wars CCG World Championship, run by the [[Players Committee]] at Gen Con in Indianapolis, Indiana, on 19–22 August 2004.<ref name="tfn-2004">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Star_Wars_CCG_2004_World_Championships_to_be_at_GenCon_83658.asp Star Wars CCG 2004 World Championships to be at GenCon], TheForce.Net (6 May 2004): "held at this year's GenCon in Indianapolis, Indiana, August 19-22"</ref><ref name="awards">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Awards and Hall of Fame], starwarsccg.org; Wayback [https://web.archive.org/web/20230817222457/https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ 17 August 2023]</ref><ref name="pc-2004">[http://www.swccgpc.com/interior.htm SWCCGPC.com] (World Championship at Gen Con Indy, 19–22 August 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040710155145/http://www.swccgpc.com/interior.htm Internet Archive, 10 July 2004]</ref> [[Brandon Schele]] defeated [[Reid Smith]] in the final.<ref name="awards" /> Schele posted his Dark [[My Lord, Is That Legal? / I Will Make It Legal|My Lord, Is That Legal?]] and Light [[Yavin 4: Massassi Throne Room]] decks on DeckTech as his "World Champion" lists (see Results). The field size and places 3–8 have not been found.

The constructed pool was printed Decipher cards through [[Theed Palace]] plus the original [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)|Players Committee Virtual Sets]] then legal. The wiki files it under [[Premiere - Original VS6]], from the newest virtual cards in the published lists; a numbered cutoff for the event has not been confirmed.

Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012152200/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t75427.html Internet Archive]</ref> Decks are the lists recovered in 2026 from DeckTech posts (Internet Archive copies) and Players Committee decklist forms; each deck page cites its own source.
